# Vienna 1683 – Economy & finance

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/europe-1683-vienna.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Coinage (stamped metal money)** [`coinage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coinage.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Accounts run in Gulden of 60 Kreuzer; Reichstaler and ducats are the big coins. Small silver has been debased under Leopold. Church silver is seized for coin in the siege. Local: Vienna mint; assayers and goldsmiths; silver and gold from Kremnitz and Schemnitz (Lower Hungary).
- **Double-entry bookkeeping** [`double_entry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/double_entry.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Wholesale merchants keep Italian double-entry books. The Hofkammer and the estates use charge-and-discharge accounts, which hide the total debt. Local: Niederlagsverwandte; Hofbuchhalterei.
- **Interest-bearing loans, pledges and limits on debt bondage** [`interest_loans_collateral`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interest_loans_collateral.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept medium. Interest of 5 to 6 percent is lawful and usual; the crown pays far more through discounts. Since the 1670 expulsion small pawn credit is scarce. Local: Samuel Oppenheimer; monasteries and endowments as lenders; estates' credit.
- **Deposit banking and bills of exchange** [`banking_credit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/banking_credit.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. No public bank: the Banco del Giro comes in 1703 and the Wiener Stadtbank in 1706. Wholesalers and court factors move money by bills on Nuremberg, Augsburg, Venice and Amsterdam. Local: Samuel Oppenheimer (court factor); Niederlagsverwandte. Elsewhere: Amsterdam Wisselbank (1609); Hamburg Bank (1619); Venice Banco del Giro; Nuremberg Banco Publico (1621).
- **Paper money** [`paper_money`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/paper_money.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. The Stockholm notes of 1661 collapsed within years. After the coin debasement of the 1620s people trust only metal. The Hofkammer pays suppliers in assignments on future revenue. Elsewhere: Stockholm: Palmstruch's notes (1661–1664); London: goldsmiths' notes.
- **Money supply, debasement and inflation** [`quantity_theory_inflation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quantity_theory_inflation.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The Kipper und Wipper debasement of the 1620s is remembered as fraud by coiners. Bodin's link between American silver and prices is known to jurists.
- **Risk-sharing partnership (commenda, mudaraba)** [`partnership_commenda`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/partnership_commenda.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Merchant houses, mining shares (Kuxe) and army supply contracts are run as partnerships.
- **Joint-stock company and limited liability** [`joint_stock_company`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/joint_stock_company.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. The privileged Oriental Company (1667) trades ironware and cloth down the Danube to the Ottoman lands, with court shareholders; it does poorly and the war ends it. Local: Orientalische Handelskompanie (1667). Elsewhere: Amsterdam: VOC (1602); London: East India Company.
- **Insurance (marine, fire, life)** [`insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/insurance.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Marine insurance is known from Venice and Amsterdam. In Vienna fire victims get alms and tax relief. Insuring lives would look like wagering on death. Elsewhere: London: Barbon's Fire Office (1681); Hamburg: fire fund (1676); Amsterdam: marine insurance.
- **Life tables and the pricing of annuities** [`life_tables_annuities`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/life_tables_annuities.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Life annuities are sold at flat rates regardless of age. The Vienna death registers since 1648 would allow a table; nobody has used them. Local: Totenbeschauprotokolle. Elsewhere: London: Graunt (1662); The Hague: Johan de Witt's annuity valuation (1671); Hanover: Leibniz's essays on annuities (c. 1680–83).
- **Public debt and government bonds** [`public_debt_bonds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_debt_bonds.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. The crown borrows by pledging tolls, mines and domains, through advances from court factors and loans guaranteed by the estates. Payments are late; its paper sells at steep discounts. Local: Hofkammer; Lower Austrian estates' obligations; Samuel Oppenheimer. Elsewhere: Holland: funded provincial debt at about 4 percent; Genoa, Venice.
- **Stock exchange (securities market)** [`stock_exchange`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/stock_exchange.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Merchants know the Amsterdam bourse from correspondents. Vienna has nothing to trade in one; its exchange opens in 1771. Elsewhere: Amsterdam: share trading in VOC stock, with futures and options.
- **Central bank and lender of last resort** [`central_bank`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/central_bank.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Public deposit banks abroad are known to cameralists. A bank under the Hofkammer would not be trusted; the Stadtbank of 1706 is placed under the city for that reason. Elsewhere: Stockholm: Riksens Ständers Bank (1668); Amsterdam Wisselbank.
- **Division of labour and specialisation** [`division_of_labour`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/division_of_labour.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Trades are finely divided by guild rules. Dividing one product into many simple tasks under one roof is the manufactory idea of Becher and Schröder; guilds oppose it. Local: Kunst- und Werkhaus am Tabor. Elsewhere: Holland and England: shipyards, cloth works; France: Colbert's royal manufactures.
- **Comparative advantage and free trade** [`comparative_advantage_free_trade`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/comparative_advantage_free_trade.md) — K1, use wrong, make easy, accept low. Policy aims at import bans, home manufactures and keeping coin in the land. Hörnigk states it in nine rules in 1684. Tolls divide every province from the next. Local: Philipp Wilhelm von Hörnigk; Wilhelm von Schröder.
- **Prices, supply and demand** [`price_mechanism_supply_demand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/price_mechanism_supply_demand.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Bread, meat and wine have official prices; dearness is blamed on hoarders. Siege prices are fixed on 1 August, the order is repeated almost daily, and a black market grows. Local: city market office; bakers' and butchers' guilds.
- **Public granaries and price stabilisation (ever-normal granary)** [`ever_normal_granary`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ever_normal_granary.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. The city and the army keep grain and flour magazines, filled in haste before the siege. Stocks last the two months; fresh meat and vegetables run out. Local: imperial Proviantamt; city grain stores; Bürgerspital stores and monastery cellars.
- **Income tax and progressive rates** [`progressive_income_tax`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/progressive_income_tax.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Taxes are the land Kontribution voted by the estates and passed on to peasants, excises on drink and meat, and occasional graded poll and wealth levies for Turkish wars. Elsewhere: Holland: excises and property levies.
- **Savings banks, credit and consumer cooperatives** [`cooperatives_savings_banks`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cooperatives_savings_banks.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Miners' and guild chests pool dues for sickness and burial. No place takes small savings at interest; a public pawn office opens in 1707. Elsewhere: Italy: Monti di Pietà.
- **Wealth as productivity; sustained economic growth** [`economic_growth_productivity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/economic_growth_productivity.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Cameralists equate strength with population, employment and coin kept at home. Becher called consumption the soul of trade. Wealth through cheaper production is not their idea. Local: Wilhelm von Schröder; Philipp Wilhelm von Hörnigk. Elsewhere: London: William Petty, John Locke.
- **National income accounts (GDP)** [`national_accounts_gdp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/national_accounts_gdp.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. From 1673 Becher and Hörnigk compiled trade statistics of the Austrian and Bohemian lands. Petty's political arithmetic circulates in manuscript in England. Local: Philipp Wilhelm von Hörnigk; toll and excise registers of the Hofkammer. Elsewhere: London and Dublin: William Petty.
- **Fighting slumps by sustaining demand (Keynesian policy)** [`aggregate_demand_countercyclical_policy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aggregate_demand_countercyclical_policy.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Cameralists condemn hoarding and praise circulation of money, but the treasury is empty and in arrears. Spending is war spending.
